snippet.textDisplay: 12 is fine. 24 is better if they stop with the regular season rankings system and revert back to smaller conferences so every team plays mostly, if not every team, every year. The AP and coaches and whoever can rank whatever teams they want all year as much as they want... but they shouldn't hold any weight. Give every conference champion an auto bid and let the committee choose the remaining at large... and i say that as a Notre Dame, knowing it gives everyone a chance at an autobid except us and UConn, but it just makes sense. That might even be what actually forces us into a conference. If they go 24 they should try to make 16 relatively even numbered, regional conferences or at least including schools that make sense to be in a conference together. That's 16 autobids to every conference champ and 8 at large bids based on the committee selection... our even better, bring back something similar to the BCS ranking metrics to make the standard of judgment uniform for everyone. There. Fixed. Though this will never happen and is sure to be hated by a majority for some reason or another.

snippet.textDisplay: Honest opinion? The people in control of college football will do literally anything if it means even a little more money, up to and including destroying the best parts of this game-- most notably, the traditions and the regular season. Let's say Georgia's 11-0 (or this year, 9-2) going into the final week of the season-- they're guaranteed a top 8 seed, why risk playing all your starters in a now meaningless game? Plus, I don't understand why we couldn't have the 12-team playoff just a little longer. The 4-team lasted a decade, why not give the 12-team seven or eight years?

Also it should be, if you don't have any top 25 (based on the final standings from BSC comp model) wins, you shouldnt get in.
